title: Understanding the Components
text: The expected squared error can be broken down into three main components: variance, bias squared, and irreducible error. Can you identify which part of the equation represents each of these components?

title: Focus on Variance
text: Consider the term E[(E[f_hat_theta(x)]-f_hat_theta(x))**2]. This term is related to the variance of the model. What does variance tell us about the model's predictions?

title: Identifying the Irreducible Error
text: Which term in the equation represents the irreducible error, which is the noise inherent in the data?

title: Exploring Bias
text: The term (h(x)-E[f_hat_theta(x)])**2 is related to the bias of the model. How does bias affect the accuracy of the model's predictions?

title: Understanding Bias
text: Which term in the equation represents the bias squared, which measures the error introduced by approximating a real-world problem?
